episodes.title: AI researchers debate what we should do next – Daniel Kokotajlo and Ege Erdil
episodes.about: Daniel Kokotajlo and Ege Erdil debate what we should do next as AI advances. Their main disagreement is how likely an intelligence explosion before 2029 is — Erdil puts it around 20%, Kokotajlo above 50% — and they agree that either way civilization needs a plan that makes sense, including not antagonizing China if a global treaty will be needed to make superintelligence go well.
episodes.why: Always-include show, out yesterday: two of the sharpest AI forecasters argue over the odds of an intelligence explosion before 2029 — 20% versus over 50% — and what anyone should actually do about it.

episodes.title: How A.I. Is Transforming Mathematics
episodes.about: Terence Tao is one of the world's leading mathematicians, and is watching — along with the rest of us — as artificial intelligence transforms his field. He joins Max this week to explain what he's been seeing. An interview with the Fields Medal winner on how the latest models are changing mathematics.
episodes.why: Out yesterday: Terence Tao on how the newest models are changing mathematics, days after the Riemann proof story — what a Fields Medalist is actually seeing from inside the field.

episodes.title: Inside the AI Training Data Market — Gabe Greenberg, G2i
episodes.about: A frontier lab can pay more for training data it gets to keep exclusive, or take a discount on data another lab can buy too. At AI Engineer CODE, G2i founder Gabe Greenberg tells swyx how labs make that decision, and how small pilot orders turn into bigger deals.
episodes.why: Out last night: how frontier labs actually buy training data — the exclusive-versus-shared price tradeoff — from G2i's founder, who sells it to them.

episodes.title: The seniors hooked on AI slop
episodes.about: Older adults are watching too many AI-generated videos and their grown children are trying to intervene. This episode is a version of Vox's The Gray Area, hosted by Miles Bryan.
episodes.why: Out yesterday: the other end of the AI video flood — seniors binging AI-generated videos while their adult kids try to intervene.

episodes.title: Claude Approves Its Own Code, Amazon Allows Meta's AI Agent
episodes.about: Anthropic just shipped Claude Ship, where Claude writes, reviews and approves its own code. Amazon is reportedly in talks to let Meta's Muse shopping agent back onto its store. Congress is lining up hearings for Jensen Huang, and Google's Gemini 4 Neon set a day-one usage record. The top AI stories right now and what people are saying about them.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — AI Breakdown is a short daily AI news show; Anthropic's Claude Ship, where Claude writes, reviews and approves its own code, plus Amazon reportedly letting Meta's Muse shopping agent back onto its store.
